---
description: "How NCodeGroup libraries design, version, track and evolve their public surface: compatibility rules, PublicAPI file tracking, visibility, open vocabularies, extensibility seams, management-API contracts and the conventions for public types and members."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.csproj, **/*.props, **/*.targets, **/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, **/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, **/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/*.tf"

# Public API

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **After a package's first stable (GA) release, change its public surface only by adding to it. Do not remove, rename, or change the parameters, return type, nullability or semantics of a shipped public or protected member in place. Add a new overload instead, and save breaking changes for a major version bump.** Shipped surface is a contract that consumers compile and bind against. Any in-place change breaks them without warning. *Check:* In a released package, look for parameters added, removed or retyped on existing public or protected members, `?` toggled on public parameters, returns or properties, changed or removed lines in PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, or `*REMOVED*` entries, all without a major version bump. *Note:* Nullability (`string` ↔ `string?`) counts as part of the signature. Before the first stable release, the pre-release rule below applies instead. <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity .claude/commands/review-code.md</sub>
- **Before removing a shipped public type or member, mark it `[Obsolete("…", error: false)]` in a minor release and keep it working. Remove it only in a later major version.** Deprecating first warns consumers and gives them a way to migrate before the breaking removal. *Check:* Look for shipped public members deleted without an earlier Obsolete stage or outside a major bump, and for `[Obsolete(..., error: true)]` added in a minor release. *Note:* Pre-1.0 packages skip this cycle (see the pre-release clean-cutover rule). <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md</sub>
- **Do not break stored data formats or serialized contracts silently. When a change to persisted entities, schemas or serialized shapes is unavoidable, ship an explicit migration with it.** Existing persisted data and wire payloads outlive the code. A silent format change corrupts or orphans them. *Check:* Look for changes to persisted entities, schemas, JSON property names or serialized discriminators that have no migration or compatibility handling. <sub>Identity .claude/commands/review-code.md</sub>
- **Append new members to public or serialized enums with new values. Never reorder, renumber or reuse existing values, and never insert a member mid-list in a way that shifts implicit numbering.** Renumbering changes the meaning of values already stored or sent on the wire. *Check:* Look for enum diffs that change explicit values or order, or that insert a member in the middle without explicit values. <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md</sub>
- **On public types, take required inputs as constructor parameters and add optional inputs as nullable `init` properties whose default the library resolves internally (fail-closed). Never add an optional input as a new constructor parameter, even one with a default value.** A new constructor parameter is a binary-breaking change for every call site and serializer. A nullable init property is purely additive. *Check:* Look for new parameters on existing public constructors for optional values, and for optional init properties whose default the consumer is expected to supply. <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Model a growing set of optional filter, selection or pagination criteria as a single criteria parameter: a `readonly record struct` with non-`required`, init-only properties, no positional constructor, built with object initializers or `with`. Keep the required keys that scope the operation as positional parameters.** New criteria can then be added without changing the method signature. Positional or `required` criteria would make each addition breaking again. *Check:* Look for public or store methods that gain another optional or nullable filter parameter, criteria types declared positionally or as mutable classes or with `required`/settable members, criteria built through constructor arguments, and a required scoping key folded into the DTO. <sub>Identity ADR-0099; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give public validator and service operations a request object, and give public configuration callbacks a single growable options type (for example `Action<TOptions>`), instead of loose primitive or delegate parameters.** New fields and settings can then be added as properties without breaking callers. *Check:* Look for new public validation methods that take several primitive parameters, and for public methods that add another delegate parameter or delegate argument instead of extending the options type. <sub>Identity ADR-0274; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md</sub>
- **Make an extensibility interface async from the start if a plausible replacement implementation would need IO.** Changing a synchronous signature to async later is a breaking change. *Check:* Look for new replaceable policy or resolver interfaces with synchronous methods that real implementations would back with a database or remote lookup. <sub>Identity ADR-0091</sub>
- **Before a package's first stable release, keep PublicAPI.Shipped.txt empty and list the whole surface in PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt. Make breaking changes as a clean cutover with no shims, `[Obsolete]` forwarders, legacy aliases or dual code paths, and remove broken public values (such as discriminators no handler can round-trip) outright. Move the surface to Shipped.txt at the first stable release, after which the compatibility rules apply in full.** With no released consumers, deprecation cycles buy nothing, and a half-migrated design with two sources of truth is the worse outcome. *Check:* In a pre-1.0 package, look for entries added to Shipped.txt, compatibility shims or fallback branches that read both old and new shapes, and public constants or discriminators with no handler. Do not object to a pre-release rename or reshaped contract only because it breaks compatibility; judge its design instead. In a stable release, flag surface still only listed in Unshipped.txt. *Note:* This overrides the Obsolete-first and additive-only rules for pre-1.0 packages only. <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity ADR-0025; Identity ADR-0105</sub>
- **Every packable project must reference Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers and keep a PublicAPI.Shipped.txt/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt pair. Record every public addition, including new public abstract or virtual hooks and both the container and member lines of a C# extension member, in Unshipped.txt. Mark removals with a `*REMOVED*` prefix instead of deleting lines, remove stale entries, keep the files LF, and edit Shipped.txt only at release time.** The analyzer makes every surface change show up in the diff, so accidental API changes get caught. Shipped.txt is the baseline for the next release. *Check:* Look for new packable projects without the files or that opt out of the analyzer, public changes without a matching Unshipped.txt diff, deleted lines in place of `*REMOVED*`, stale entries, CRLF rewrites, and Shipped.txt edits outside a release. <sub>Identity ADR-0005; Identity ADR-0009; Identity ADR-0053; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give every type and member the narrowest visibility that works. Make something public only for a stated consumer-facing reason, never for tests, and never add `public virtual` or leave a public type unsealed just so it can be mocked.** An accidental public member is a SemVer contract that only a major-version obsoletion cycle can remove. A public virtual member is also an override point that a subclass could use to weaken security controls. *Check:* Look for new public types or members without a consumer-facing reason, members widened to public, protected or virtual only for tests, and public concrete classes that are unsealed but not designed for subclassing. *Note:* Use `internal virtual` for one-off override seams, and leave internal implementation classes unsealed so they can be mocked. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give tests access to internals through `InternalsVisibleTo` for the test assembly (plus `DynamicProxyGenAssembly2` for Moq) only. Never use `InternalsVisibleTo` to let one production assembly use another's internals; make packages collaborate through designed public contracts.** Cross-assembly internals access is hidden coupling that PublicApiAnalyzers does not track, so a refactor that is safe in one assembly can break another. *Check:* Look for `InternalsVisibleTo` attributes or csproj items that target a non-test production assembly. <sub>Identity ADR-0004; Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Mark a type or member that is public only for infrastructure collaboration between sibling packages with `[EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)]`, and start its `<summary>` with "This API supports the ... infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code."** Following the EF Core / ASP.NET Core pattern, the collaboration surface stays explicit and version-tracked without showing up in application IntelliSense. *Check:* Look for new public members that exist only for sibling packages but lack the attribute or the standard summary sentence. <sub>Identity ADR-0004</sub>
- **Expose a replaceable service as a public interface and make its single canonical DI-resolved implementation an `internal` class named `DefaultFoo` for interface `IFoo`, reached only through the interface.** Integrators extend the library by implementing the interface, not by depending on or subclassing the default. This follows the ASP.NET Core idiom and keeps the surface small. *Check:* Look for a public `Default*` class, or for a sole DI-registered implementation of `IFoo` named `FooService`, `FooImpl` or plain `Foo`. <sub>Identity ADR-0006; Identity ADR-0015; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Reserve the `Default` prefix for the one canonical DI implementation. Name each variant implementation for what makes it specific, name implementations of framework interfaces by the framework's own pattern, and give public data, message, model or result types that consumers construct directly the bare concept name, even when they implement an interface.** `Default*` signals an internal, replaceable default. On any other type it misleads consumers and takes the clean concept name. *Check:* Look for public models, DTOs or results named `Default*`, and for one of several implementations of an interface named just `DefaultFoo`. <sub>Identity ADR-0006; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make concrete dispatch jobs, handlers, envelope formats, key-derivation and master-key details, and other implementation mechanics internal. Expose only the abstraction that consumers program against.** Internal mechanics can then evolve, for example through master-key rotation or a new envelope layout, without breaking consumers. *Check:* Look for new public job or handler classes that only their own package dispatches, and for public types exposing envelope layout, master keys, derivation or root wrapper implementations. <sub>Identity ADR-0090; Identity ADR-0235</sub>
- **Put a security policy that every implementation must apply behind its own public, replaceable interface with an internal default, which other replaceable services resolve and call. Do not embed the policy inside a replaceable default implementation or a data resolver.** Otherwise anyone who replaces the implementation must reimplement the policy or silently skips it, and an extension cannot tighten a bound without replacing the whole service. *Check:* Look for enforcement logic that is internal to the default implementation of a public replaceable interface, or inside a resolver meant only to supply data, with no separate policy seam. <sub>Identity ADR-0158; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Model a one-time secret reveal as a separate create-only response type that extends the metadata resource. Never add an optional or nullable secret or material property to the resource type that read and list paths return.** A usually-null secret field on a shared read type turns leakage prevention into a matter of review discipline. A separate type guarantees it by construction. *Check:* Look for a secret, value or material property added to a DTO that GET or list endpoints return, and for read endpoints declared to return the reveal type. <sub>Identity ADR-0050</sub>
- **Never expose internal surrogate keys (such as snowflake `long` ids) on the wire. Use only the opaque string identifier externally.** Surrogate keys are storage internals, and snowflakes also leak creation time and ordering. *Check:* Look for DTOs, routes or responses that carry an entity's surrogate key. <sub>Identity ADR-0014</sub>
- **Have the server generate the identifier of a resource it creates and return it in the 201 Created body and Location header. Do not accept the new resource's id in the create request. Caller-supplied references to existing parent resources are fine, and tenants are the exception: the creator chooses a tenant's id, and the id is then immutable, with editable labels kept in a separate display-name field.** Opaque server ids stay meaningless anchors for foreign keys, tokens and audit records. A tenant id is part of the public issuer and hostname, so it must be known up front and never change. *Check:* Look for non-tenant create DTOs with an Id for the new resource, handlers that persist a caller-provided id, 201 responses without the generated id or Location header, create-tenant paths that generate the id, and update-tenant contracts or logic that can change it. *Note:* A later ADR may approve other specific exceptions, such as a requested DCR-style client_id. <sub>Identity ADR-0014; Identity ADR-0159</sub>
- **Do not expose generic query protocols (OData, JSON:API filter/sort/expand) or `IQueryable`/expressions above the persistence layer. Add each filter as an explicit named parameter, backed by an explicit store method and an indexed column, within keyset pagination.** Arbitrary queries leak `IQueryable` across the store boundary, create denial-of-service risk through unindexed sorts and N+1 expands, and become a heavy versioned contract. *Check:* Look for OData packages, `$filter`/`$orderby`/`$expand` handling, stores that return or accept `IQueryable` or expressions, and filters on unindexed columns. <sub>Identity ADR-0019; Identity ADR-0022</sub>
- **Page collections with keyset pagination, ordered by the sort key plus a unique identifier as tie-breaker and backed by an index on those columns. Use opaque cursors that only the persistence layer creates and reads, holding the last item's sort key and id, and pass them through the web layer unchanged.** A non-unique sort key such as a timestamp alone produces duplicates or gaps. An opaque, store-owned cursor keeps the boundary intact and lets the encoding change. *Check:* Look for offset paging, sorts on a non-unique timestamp alone, cursors without the tie-breaker, web code that decodes or builds cursors, and contracts that expose raw key fields as the continuation mechanism. <sub>Identity ADR-0019; Identity ADR-0303</sub>
- **Treat API time-range filters as half-open: start inclusive, end exclusive.** Adjacent ranges then neither overlap nor leave gaps, matching the API's convention. *Check:* Look for range filters using `<=` on the end or `>` on the start. <sub>Identity ADR-0303</sub>
- **Do not map a literal segment directly under a collection whose next segment is an id (for example `/api/tenants/check-address` beside `/api/tenants/{id}`). Expose the operation as a sub-resource or at a separate path.** The literal collides with `/{id}`, so the request may be answered as a lookup of a resource with that name. *Check:* Look for new `/{collection}/{literal}` routes next to an existing `/{collection}/{id}` route. <sub>Identity ADR-0165; Identity ADR-0233</sub>
- **Make a preview or dry-run endpoint call the same validation seam as the write it previews, and authorize it as a read when the resource exists and as a create when it does not.** The preview's verdict then matches what the write will decide, and the preview cannot be used to get around create authorization. *Check:* Look for previews that duplicate validation logic, or that use one fixed authorization policy regardless of whether the resource exists. <sub>Identity ADR-0165</sub>
- **Make a once-only state transition (revoking a grant, terminating sessions, add-if-absent) report what this call actually did: a `bool` for one item (false when the item is unknown, belongs to another tenant or was already transitioned, including by a concurrent caller) or a count for bulk. Report and audit that result, not a count taken beforehand. Name add-if-absent operations with a `Try` prefix.** Callers need to know whether their call made the change. A count taken before the operation overstates it when a concurrent request got there first. *Check:* Look for revoke or add methods that return void or throw when the item is missing or already transitioned, bool-returning add methods without a `Try` prefix, and endpoints or audits that count before revoking. <sub>Identity ADR-0215; Identity ADR-0227; Identity ADR-0284</sub>
- **Model any vocabulary that a consumer, deployment or sibling package could ever need to extend (reasons, kinds, formats, failure codes, outcomes, categories, scopes, protocol values such as grant types) as an open set: `public const string` well-known names in a static class, or registered named strategies or descriptors resolved through a catalog, or an open type with well-known static instances. Compare names ordinally and keep the documented casing (lower-case, snake_case for codes). Pass unknown-but-registered names through unchanged.** An enum or closed set fixes members at compile time, so every extension would need an edit to the core library. *Check:* Look for new enums or closed switches for extensible kinds, reasons, formats or protocol values, validation that rejects registered values not among the predefined constants, handlers that rewrite unknown names, and case-insensitive or culture-sensitive name comparisons. <sub>Identity ADR-0098; Identity ADR-0104; Identity ADR-0150; Identity ADR-0172; Identity ADR-0181; Identity ADR-0206; Identity ADR-0276; Identity ADR-0278; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Introduce an `enum` only when something outside extension fixes its members: a finite list from an external specification implemented in full, the outcome set of one library-owned operation, or a mirror of a framework type. No other package could ever need another member.** The question is whether another package could ever need to add a member, not whether this library owns the current members. A settings-scope enum, for example, shut out every extension that stores settings for an entity of its own. *Check:* For each new enum, check for that justification. Flag enums justified only by the library owning today's members. <sub>Identity ADR-0150; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Validate a requested vocabulary name against what is registered or declared supported at every entry point, and reject unregistered names with an error that lists the accepted values. Never ignore unknown names silently.** Checking at every entry point keeps behavior consistent, and an error that lists the accepted values tells the caller how to fix the request. *Check:* Look for entry points that skip the support check, unknown names that are ignored, or rejection messages that do not list the supported values. <sub>Identity ADR-0104; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not encode a vocabulary's hierarchy, compatibility, order or behavior in `[Flags]`, bit masks, exhaustive switches or hard-coded chains, and never infer a trait from a name (equality, prefix or suffix). Make relationships registered data, and have each pluggable strategy declare its traits through a member.** Relationships encoded in code are lock-in even when the names are strings, and third-party strategies could not get the same behavior. *Check:* Look for `[Flags]` on extensible concepts, exhaustive switches over vocabulary names, `StartsWith`/`EndsWith` tests on names, and code like `MethodName == "tls_client_auth"` that decides behavior. <sub>Identity ADR-0150; Identity ADR-0288; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Report failures and reasons as machine-readable codes from an open vocabulary, and have callers branch on those codes, never on exception or error message text. Give validation violations in an open vocabulary their own human-readable description that names the values involved, and have callers report that description.** Codes can grow without breaking consumers, while message text changes freely and cannot be matched reliably. *Check:* Look for code that inspects message strings to decide behavior, closed enums of violation kinds that extensions would need to extend, and callers that build their own messages from a kind. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-0206; Identity ADR-0278</sub>
- **Give a validation result a nullable failure code that defines validity (`IsValid => FailureCode is null`), with a failure constructor that requires a non-empty code and a non-empty reason. Annotate boolean status properties on result types with `[MemberNotNullWhen]` naming the error members they guarantee.** Validity then cannot disagree with the code, and callers get correct nullability flow for the error members. *Check:* Look for result types with a separate validity flag that could disagree with the code, failure constructors that accept missing or empty arguments, and boolean status properties next to nullable error members without `[MemberNotNullWhen]`. <sub>Identity ADR-0278; Identity ADR-0236</sub>
- **Make a public catalog or registry `internal` when a specification fixes its entries to a closed set (for example the RFC 8032 curves or the FIPS 204 ML-DSA parameter sets), and let callers select an entry by its standard identifier (`crv`, `alg`). Expose a public extensible catalog only when the set is open by nature.** Adding to a spec-closed set would define a different algorithm, so a public extension point would be meaningless surface. *Check:* Look for new public or consumer-extensible registries whose entries a specification fixes. <sub>Identity ADR-0117; Identity ADR-0118</sub>
- **Do not model an extensible event or record family as a closed polymorphic `[JsonDerivedType]` hierarchy that lists every subtype on the base type.** A package that adds an event must not have to edit the base library. *Check:* Look for `[JsonDerivedType]` attributes enumerating event or record subtypes on a shared base type. <sub>Identity ADR-0283</sub>
- **Model protocol responses and documents whose members vary by token, host, scope or extension (introspection, UserInfo, discovery, capabilities) with the fixed required members as properties and everything else in a `[JsonExtensionData]` dictionary flattened into the top-level JSON. Build discovery-style documents from registered contributor providers.** New claims or sections can then be added by registering a provider, with no public-API change to the type or the endpoint. *Check:* Look for new strongly-typed properties for optional or host-defined claims on such responses, and for discovery sections added by editing the resource type or endpoint instead of registering a provider. <sub>Identity ADR-0029; Identity ADR-0030; Identity ADR-0067</sub>
- **Take extension protocol parameters (such as `prompt`, `max_age`, `login_hint`) through an open dictionary copied with `StringComparer.Ordinal`, not fixed fields. When the dictionary is set, reject with `ArgumentException` empty names and the names the client writes itself or that would break the flow (`response_type`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `nonce`, `scope`, `resource`, `response_mode`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`, `request_uri`, `client_secret`, `client_assertion`, `client_assertion_type`, `dpop_jkt`). Add each new client-written parameter to that reserved list.** The protocol vocabulary is open, but a caller must not be able to override parameters the client controls. *Check:* Look for fixed properties added for extension parameters, missing or late reserved-name or empty-name checks, client-written parameters missing from the reserved list, and non-ordinal dictionary copies. <sub>Identity ADR-0275; Identity ADR-0286</sub>
- **Define event payloads as immutable `record` or `readonly record struct` types with typed fields, with no object-valued metadata bags (`IDictionary<string, object>`, property bags, `[JsonExtensionData]`). Publish plain events directly with `PublishAsync(new FooEvent(...))`, and add a typed helper only when it builds a shared envelope or uses a subscriber short-circuit.** Bags make events mutable and let secrets or PII slip past redaction. Trivial publish wrappers add tracked surface and give nothing in return. *Check:* Look for mutable event classes or object-valued bags on events, and for new public helpers that only construct an event and publish it. <sub>Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **Keep a pluggable seam limited to its core operations. Put capabilities that only some backends support (lockout, two-factor, password change) on separate optional interfaces that consumers probe for, and split an interface whose consumers use disjoint sets of operations (for example an encoder and a validator). Keep one persisted concept behind one backend seam rather than several interfaces split by verb.** Segregated interfaces, as in ASP.NET Core Identity, let capabilities be added without reworking shipped surface or making backends stub out members, while one seam per concept spares backend authors from implementing several overlapping interfaces. *Check:* Look for optional-feature members added to a widely implemented core interface, combined interfaces where each consumer uses only one part, and new read/verify/write interfaces over the same entity that a backend would have to implement together. <sub>Identity ADR-0051; Identity ADR-0230; Identity ADR-0120; Identity ADR-0060</sub>
- **Give shared abstractions (such as audit recorders) one generic, capability-agnostic entry point that takes a caller-defined subtype. Do not add a method or constants for each capability, and do not add empty marker interfaces for roles that are filled by selecting a registered implementation by name.** Per-capability members couple a general abstraction to one feature's shape, and a role marker adds a type without adding a rule. *Check:* Look for methods on shared interfaces named after or typed to one feature, feature-specific event types or constants in base abstractions packages, and empty interfaces such as `IRootXxx : IXxx` that only mark a configurable role. <sub>Identity ADR-0061; Identity ADR-0279</sub>
- **Model a configurable, extensible set of rules the way ASP.NET Core authorization does: pure-data requirement records, interpreted by handlers keyed by requirement type and resolved from DI as a collection. Do not use opaque closures or a fluent DSL that holds the logic.** The configuration stays declarative and inspectable, and third parties can add rules by registering a handler without forking. *Check:* Look for validation configuration built from closures or a logic-bearing DSL, and for fixed built-in rule sets with no requirement-plus-handler extension point. <sub>Identity ADR-0120</sub>
- **Put helpers that extension authors need (merge or combinator helpers for descriptors) in the public abstractions package, and keep the default implementations that use them internal. Do not require constructor dependencies on a public extensible base class that only some derived families use; inject them on the intermediate base that uses them.** Helpers on internal types cannot be reused by external authors, and dependencies on the base couple every extender to primitives it does not need. *Check:* Look for `public static` helpers that extensions need but that sit on internal or implementation-package types, and for unused constructor parameters on public extensibility base classes. <sub>Identity ADR-0038; Identity ADR-0105</sub>
- **When a member is added to a record or result type that extension implementations fill in, and each implementation must choose its value, declare the member `required`.** Every implementation, third-party ones included, then decides on a value deliberately instead of silently getting a default. *Check:* Look for new optional or defaulted members on extension-populated descriptors where each implementation must make a choice. *Note:* On types that already shipped, adding a `required` member is breaking for consumers that construct them. Prefer it pre-1.0 or in a major release. Criteria DTOs must not use `required`. <sub>Identity ADR-0268</sub>
- **When an operation's behavior depends on a context its input cannot reliably convey, require that context as an explicit parameter, reject unknown values with `ArgumentException`, and offer no overload that omits it. When a validation runs outside a protocol request, pass `null` for the (nullable) request and skip the request-specific checks instead of building a fake request.** Inferring the context from the shape of the data guesses wrong exactly where it matters, and a fake request pretends there is a request when there is none. *Check:* Look for methods that guess scope from data shape, overloads that default away a needed context, missing `ArgumentException` for unrecognized values, and dummy request objects built only to call a validator. <sub>Identity ADR-0148; Identity ADR-0225</sub>
- **Keep tenant-bound or context-bound services bound to their context. To target another tenant, materialize a context for it instead of adding overloads that take a tenant id.** Overloads fork the service surface, and downstream machinery still needs a materialized context anyway. *Check:* Look for new overloads on context-bound services that take a `tenantId` to bypass the bound context. <sub>Identity ADR-0100</sub>
- **Attach type information and per-type rules to the object or collection they describe, at construction or parse time (through constructor and `Parse` overloads). Do not add methods that re-type items afterwards, or overloads that make every caller look up the descriptor again.** An object then keeps its rules when it crosses a boundary, items are not built twice, and callers cannot hold an untyped instance by mistake. *Check:* Look for methods like `WithKeyTypes(...)` that rebuild a parsed collection, and for `Method(descriptor)` overloads whose data the object could carry itself. <sub>Identity ADR-0271; Identity ADR-0281</sub>
- **Use public constructors on model types to adopt an in-memory value (`JsonElement`, `JsonObject`, a collection), and a static `Parse(string)` method to deserialize text.** A consistent verb split tells callers whether input is adopted or parsed. *Check:* Look for constructors that take raw JSON text, and for `Parse`/`From*` factories that only wrap an in-memory node or collection. <sub>Identity ADR-0119</sub>
- **Make a wrapper or overload that claims to behave like an existing API honor every option it accepts, or throw `NotSupportedException` for options it cannot honor. Never ignore an option silently.** A JSON wrapper that dropped `AllowDuplicateProperties` accepted duplicate members even though its documentation said it would not. *Check:* Look for option objects copied field by field with fields left out. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Make data, options, context and event types sealed, with init or get-only members and concrete buffered collection properties (`List<T>`, not `IList<T>`). Give options classes `IValidateOptions` validators, and add interfaces only for replaceable DI seams or read-only slices.** This is AOT-friendly, cheap to re-enumerate, and free of deferred-execution surprises, and options are checked before use. *Check:* Look for unsealed DTOs or options, settable members, interface-typed collection properties on data types, and options without a validator. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Type parameters and computed return values that do not transfer ownership as the narrowest read-only interface (`IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>`). Prefer `params IEnumerable<T>` over `params T[]` and buffer inside the method. Return empty collections, not `null`, where an empty form exists.** Callers are not coupled to concrete types, and null-for-empty forces null checks on every caller and invites NullReferenceExceptions. *Check:* Look for concrete collection parameters, new `params T[]`, and methods that return or accept `null` where an empty value would do. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Have interface methods that produce output write into a `Span<T>`/`Memory<T>` destination and return a count, or into a generic `ref TWriter ... allows ref struct` writer with a sizing method beside it, instead of returning a new array. Put the input or source parameter first and the destination last.** This avoids allocation, lets callers size buffers up front, and matches existing source-first APIs such as `CopyPlaintext(source, destination)`. *Check:* Look for new interface methods that return `byte[]`, and for methods whose first parameter is a writer, buffer writer or destination span. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #382</sub>
- **Represent HTTP status codes in public models and response wrappers as `int`, not `System.Net.HttpStatusCode`.** The enum cannot name every status a server may send (such as 499), so values would not be preserved faithfully. *Check:* Look for `HttpStatusCode`-typed properties, parameters or fields in new models, except code that builds or reads `HttpResponseMessage` directly. <sub>Identity review of #320</sub>
- **Do not add a parameter that only duplicates information already available from another argument. For example, read endpoint metadata from `HttpContext.GetEndpoint()` instead of taking an endpoint name next to the `HttpContext`.** A redundant parameter can disagree with the authoritative source. *Check:* Look for methods that take both an `HttpContext` and an endpoint name or endpoint argument derivable from it. <sub>Identity review of #382</sub>
- **Do not add bool or enum parameters whose only job is to switch a method between behaviors; split it into intention-revealing methods. Likewise, use a separate validator contract for each token type with different required claims or `typ`, instead of a mode flag.** Flag parameters hide intent at call sites and produce conditional rules. *Check:* Look for flag parameters that select between branches, and for token-kind parameters or conditional claim requirements added to an existing validator. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0274</sub>
- **Do not add speculative public surface: no settings that control nothing that matters (such as body-size limits on a call whose body is discarded), and no public type shared between two independently versioned packages. Keep such a type in one owning package or duplicate it deliberately.** Unused settings are permanent surface, and shared types across independently versioned packages create diamond dependency conflicts. *Check:* Look for new options properties on paths where they have no effect, and for new shared public types used in the public surface of several independently versioned packages. <sub>Identity ADR-0111; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md</sub>
- **In key- or secret-describing contracts, include `kid` as a required, non-nullable field already resolved to its fallback.** A nullable `kid` makes every caller repeat the fallback logic, and keys are selected by `kid` either way. *Check:* Look for key or secret response DTOs that omit `kid` or declare it nullable or optional. <sub>Identity ADR-0186</sub>
- **Treat a public type's namespace as a stable contract. Do not change it when files move, and keep public types flat under the package root namespace, except options, which go in a `.Options` sub-namespace.** Reorganizing folders must not cause breaking namespace churn for consumers. *Check:* Look for public types whose namespace changed only because the file moved, and for public types in folder-based sub-namespaces other than `.Options`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Name interfaces for their role and let the namespace supply the brand. Add a qualifier only when the bare role noun would collide with a well-known BCL or framework type or is too generic. Use established acronym casing consistently (for example `DPoP`, never `Dpop`).** Role names are short and clear, and consistent casing keeps identifiers matching the existing protocol constants. *Check:* Look for needless brand prefixes, bare names that collide with common BCL types, and identifiers containing `Dpop`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0286</sub>
- **Annotate public types that are consumed by reflection, DI, the serializer or the options binder with JetBrains `[PublicAPI]`, and never apply it to internal types.** It states the intent and silences unused-member analyzers without pragmas. On an internal type it would wrongly present the type as public surface. *Check:* Look for serializer- or DI-consumed public types without `[PublicAPI]`, and for internal types that have it. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a concrete type implements two unrelated receiver interfaces (such as `IDictionary<,>` and `IReadOnlyDictionary<,>`), write one extension method on their common base and fast-path the specific interfaces inside it, not one overload per interface.** Parallel overloads make every call on the concrete type ambiguous (CS0121), and moving them into separate classes does not fix it. *Check:* Look for parallel extension overloads on `IDictionary<,>` and `IReadOnlyDictionary<,>` or similar pairs. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **For a TypeScript string vocabulary that the backend treats as open, type it as the known literals plus `(string & {})`, not as a closed union, unless it is provably closed.** A closed union turns every new value into a library edit, while the open form still autocompletes the known names. *Check:* Look for string literal unions for surfaces, kinds or types that the backend maps through an open dictionary and that lack `| (string & {})`. <sub>Identity ADR-0156</sub>
- **Keep element ids, field names and `autocomplete` values identical between server-rendered pages and the client components that replace them, and treat them as a contract.** Client bundles, automation and browser autofill all depend on these names whether or not the bundle has loaded. *Check:* Look for changes to ids, names or `autocomplete` values on only one side of a server page and its client component. <sub>Identity ADR-0253</sub>
- **Treat an infrastructure module's variables and outputs as its public API. Removing or renaming a variable or output, adding a required input, or forcing resource replacement is a breaking change that needs migration notes. When a refactor changes resource addresses, add `moved` or `removed` blocks.** Consumers must act on such changes, and forced replacement destroys live resources. *Check:* Look for removed or renamed variables or outputs, new variables without defaults, and renamed resources, module moves or changed `count`/`for_each` keys with no `moved`/`removed` block or breaking-change note. <sub>Identity ADR-0133</sub>
